_meta.indication: COTELLIC is indicated for the treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600E or V600K mutation, in combination with vemurafenib.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, international, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; all patients received vemurafenib and were randomized to cobimetinib or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: Previously untreated, BRAF V600 mutation-positive unresectable or metastatic melanoma, with mutation detected by the cobas 4800 BRAF V600 mutation test.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Investigator-assessed progression-free survival (PFS) per RECIST v1.1.
pivotal_trials.n: N=495 (247 cobimetinib plus vemurafenib; 248 placebo plus vemurafenib).
pivotal_trials.result: PFS HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.45, 0.70), p<0.001; median PFS 12.3 vs 7.2 months. OS (interim analysis) HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.47, 0.85), p=0.0019 (statistical significance judged against an allocated alpha of 0.019 for this interim analysis), median OS NE vs 17.0 months. ORR 70% vs 50%.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥20%) are diarrhea, photosensitivity reaction, nausea, pyrexia, and vomiting. Diarrhea 60% vs 31% and nausea 41% vs 25%. Serious identified risks include serous retinopathy (26% of patients) and Grade 3 or 4 liver laboratory abnormalities.
target_moa: Cobimetinib is a reversible, non-ATP-competitive inhibitor of MEK1 and MEK2, upstream regulators of the ERK pathway which promotes cellular proliferation.

boxed_warning.content: A boxed warning was not proposed and the review team did not identify safety issues requiring a boxed warning.

companion_dx_detail: cobas 4800 BRAF V600 mutation test, used to detect BRAF V600 mutation for patient selection.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because this drug is not the first in its class and the data did not raise unexpected safety or efficacy issues.

basis.text: On August 15, 2014, FDA designated as a Fast Track Development program the investigation of cobimetinib and vemurafenib for BRAF V600E-mutation positive, unresectable or metastatic melanoma to demonstrate improved PFS and OS.

summary.text: Cobimetinib received orphan drug designation (January 31, 2014) and fast track designation (August 15, 2014), and the NDA was granted priority review; approval was based on the single Phase III trial GO28141 (coBRIM) demonstrating improved PFS.
